# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name

- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event

- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event

- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id

WITH qualifying_events AS (
  SELECT attendance.link_to_event
  FROM attendance
  GROUP BY attendance.link_to_event
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT attendance.link_to_member) > 10
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS meeting_event_count
FROM event
INNER JOIN qualifying_events ON event.event_id = qualifying_events.event_id
WHERE event.type = 'Meeting'

forge.sql:
WITH yearly_budget AS (
  SELECT SUM(budget.amount) AS total_amount
  FROM budget
  INNER JOIN event ON budget.link_to_event = event.event_id
  WHERE budget.category = 'Advertisement' AND event.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff'
),
october_budget AS (
  SELECT SUM(budget.amount) AS total_amount
  FROM budget
  INNER JOIN event ON budget.link_to_event = event.event_id
  WHERE budget.category = 'Advertisement' AND event.event_name = 'October Meeting'
)
SELECT 1.0 * yearly_budget.total_amount / october_budget.total_amount AS times
FROM yearly_budget
CROSS JOIN october_budget

forge.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "Patient"."ID") AS count_patients
FROM Patient
INNER JOIN Laboratory ON Patient.ID = Laboratory.ID
INNER JOIN Examination ON Patient.ID = Examination.ID
WHERE Laboratory.CPK < 250 AND (Examination.KCT = '+' OR Examination.RVVT = '+' OR Examination.LAC = '+')

forge.sql:
SELECT circuits.location, circuits.lat, circuits.lng, COUNT(DISTINCT races.raceId) AS times_held
FROM circuits
INNER JOIN races ON circuits.circuitId = races.circuitId
WHERE circuits.country = 'Austria'
GROUP BY circuits.location, circuits.lat, circuits.lng
ORDER BY circuits.location ASC

SELECT superhero.superhero_name, superhero.height_cm, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY superhero.height_cm DESC) AS hero_rank

INNER JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id
WHERE publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
ORDER BY superhero.height_cm DESC

SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN alignment.alignment = 'Bad' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(superhero.id) AS percentage, SUM(CASE WHEN alignment.alignment = 'Bad' AND publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS marvel_bad_count
FROM superhero
INNER JOIN alignment ON superhero.alignment_id = alignment.id
INNER JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id

forge.sql:
WITH max_rep AS (
  SELECT MAX(users.Reputation) AS max_reputation
  FROM users
),
stats_posts AS (
  SELECT posts.Id, posts.Score
  FROM posts
  INNER JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
  INNER JOIN max_rep ON users.Reputation = max_rep.max_reputation
),
numerator AS (
  SELECT COUNT(stats_posts.Id) AS numerator
  FROM stats_posts
  WHERE stats_posts.Score > 50
),
denominator AS (
  SELECT COUNT(stats_posts.Id) AS denominator
  FROM stats_posts
)
SELECT 100.0 * numerator.numerator / denominator.denominator AS percentage
FROM numerator
CROSS JOIN denominator

FROM posts AS p

WITH avg_diff AS (
  SELECT AVG(frpm."Enrollment (K-12)" - frpm."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") AS average_difference
  FROM schools
  INNER JOIN frpm ON schools.CDSCode = frpm.CDSCode
  WHERE schools.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
)
SELECT schools.School, schools.DOCType
FROM schools
INNER JOIN frpm ON schools.CDSCode = frpm.CDSCode
CROSS JOIN avg_diff
WHERE schools.FundingType = 'Locally funded' AND frpm."Enrollment (K-12)" - frpm."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > avg_diff.average_difference

SELECT s.School, s.DOCType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN frpm AS f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
WHERE s.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > (
    SELECT AVG(f2."Enrollment (K-12)" - f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)")
    FROM schools AS s2
    JOIN frpm AS f2 ON f2.CDSCode = s2.CDSCode
    WHERE s2.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  );

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT district.district_id) AS count_districts
FROM district
INNER JOIN client ON district.district_id = client.district_id
WHERE district.A11 > 6000 AND district.A11 < 10000 AND client.gender = 'F'

SELECT DISTINCT d.account_id
FROM client AS c
JOIN disp AS d ON d.client_id = c.client_id
JOIN district AS r ON r.district_id = c.district_id
WHERE c.birth_date = (SELECT MAX(birth_date) FROM client)
  AND r.A11 = (SELECT MAX(A11) FROM district);

SELECT district.A2, ((district.A13 - district.A12) / district.A12) * 100 AS unemployment_rate_increment
FROM loan
INNER JOIN account ON loan.account_id = account.account_id
INNER JOIN district ON account.district_id = district.district_id
WHERE loan.status = 'D'

assistant.text:
SELECT DISTINCT d.A2, ((d.A13 - d.A12) / d.A12) * 100 AS unemployment_increment_percentage
FROM loan l
JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id
JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
WHERE l.status = 'D';
